The dog fence in Australia has been erected to keep out hostile invaders, in this case hordes of yellow dogs called dingoes. The empire it preserves is that of wool growers. Yet the fence casts a much broader ecological shadow. For the early explorers, a kangaroo or a wallaby sighting marked a noteworthy event. Now try not to see one. Without a native predator there is no check on the marsupial population. The kangaroos are now cursed more than the dingoes. They have become rivals of sheep, competing for water and grass. The State Governments now cull more than three million kangaroos a year to keep Australia's natural symbol from over running the pastoral lands.

Since the given function is continuous so that
$f(1+h)=f(1-h)=f(h)\text { Now } \quad f(1+h)=lt_{h \rightarrow 1} \frac{(1+h)^3-3(1+h)+2}{(1+h-1)^2}\Rightarrow \quad \operatorname{lt}_{h \rightarrow 0} \frac{1+h^3+3 h^2+3 h-3-3 h+2}{(h)^2}\therefore \quad f(x)=3$.

questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \left|\begin{array}{ccc}x+1 & x+2 & x+4 \\ x+3 & x+5 & x+5 \\ x+7 & x+10 & x+14\end{array}\right| \\ & c_1 \rightarrow c_2-c_1, c_3-c_2\end{aligned}\left|\begin{array}{ccc}-1 & -2 & x+4 \\ -2 & -3 & x+8 \\ -3 & -4 & x+14\end{array}\right|\begin{aligned} & =\left|\begin{array}{ccc}1 & 2 & x+4 \\ 2 & 3 & x+8 \\ 3 & 4 & x+14\end{array}\right| \\ & =\mathrm{R}_2-\mathrm{R}_1, \mathrm{R}_3-\mathrm{R}_2\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \left|\begin{array}{ccc}1 & 2 & x+4 \\ 1 & 1 & 4 \\ 1 & 1 & 6\end{array}\right| \\ = & \mathrm{R}_1-\mathrm{R}_2, \mathrm{R}_2-\mathrm{R}_3\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \left|\begin{array}{ccc}0 & 1 & x \\ 0 & 0 & -2 \\ 1 & 1 & 6\end{array}\right| \\ = & 1\{(-2)\}=-2 .\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
If 5 and 7 are the roots of the equation
$\left|\begin{array}{ccc}
x & 4 & 5 \\
7 & x & 7 \\
5 & 8 & x
\end{array}\right|=0$
then what is the third root?
questions.solution:
$\left|\begin{array}{lll}x & 4 & 5 \\ 7 & x & 7 \\ 5 & 8 & x\end{array}\right|=0\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow x\left(x^2-56\right)-7(4 x-40)+5(28-5 x)=0 \\ & \Rightarrow x^3-56 x-28 x+280+140-25 x=0 \\ & \Rightarrow x^3-109 x+420=0\end{aligned}$
Since 5 and 7 are the roots of the given equation so that
$x^2-12 x+35$ is a factor of the given equation, when we divide the given equation by $x^2-12 x+35$ it gives
$x+12=0\Rightarrow \quad x=-12$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: . If the matrix $A=\left(\begin{array}{ccc}2-x & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 3-x & 0 \\ -1 & -3 & -x\end{array}\right)$ is singular, then what is the solution set $S$ ?
questions.solution:
Since the matrix is singular therefore,
$\left|\begin{array}{ccc}
2-x & 1 & 1 \\
1 & 3-x & 0 \\
-1 & -3 & -x
\end{array}\right|=0\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \mathrm{R}_2 \rightarrow\left(\mathrm{R}_3+\mathrm{R}_2\right) \\ & \left|\begin{array}{ccc}2-x & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 3-x & 0 \\ 0 & -x & -x\end{array}\right|=0\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \left.\Rightarrow(2-x)\left\{-3 x+x^2\right)\right\}-1(-x+x)=0 \\ & \Rightarrow(2-x)\left(x^2-3 x\right)=0 \\ & \Rightarrow x(2-x),(x-3)=0 \\ & \Rightarrow x=0, x=2, x=3\end{aligned}$

questions.q: If sum of squares of the roots of the equation $x^2+k x-b=0$ is $2 b$, what is $k$ equal to?
questions.solution:
Let $\alpha, \beta$ be two roots then
$\begin{array}{rlrl} 
& & \alpha^2+\beta_2 & =2 b \text { (given) } \\
\text { Now } & & \alpha+\beta & =-\frac{k}{1}=-k \\
& & & =\frac{-b}{1}=-b \\
\Rightarrow & & \alpha^2+\beta^2 & =(\alpha+\beta)^2-2 \alpha \beta \\
\Rightarrow & & 2 b & =k^2-2(-b) \\
\Rightarrow & & 2 b & =k^2+2 b \\
\Rightarrow & k^2 & =0 \Rightarrow k=0 .
\end{array}$

questions.q: If $\frac{1}{b-a}+\frac{1}{b-c}=\frac{1}{a}+\frac{1}{c}$ then $a, b, c$ are in
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \text { Given } \quad \frac{1}{b-a}+\frac{1}{b-c}=\frac{1}{a}+\frac{1}{c} \\ & \Rightarrow \quad \frac{1}{b-a}-\frac{1}{c}=\frac{1}{a}-\frac{1}{b-c} \\ & \Rightarrow \quad \frac{c-b+a}{(b-a) c}=\frac{b-c-a}{a(b-c)} \\ & \Rightarrow \quad \frac{c-b+a}{(b-a) c}=\frac{-(c-b+a)}{a(b-c)}\end{aligned}\begin{aligned}
\Rightarrow & a(b-c) & =-(b-a) c \\
\Rightarrow & a b-a c & =-b c+a c \\
\Rightarrow & b(a+c) & =2 a c \\
\Rightarrow & b & =\frac{2 a c}{a+c} .
\end{aligned}$
Clearly $a, b, c$ are in H.P.

Which term of the series
$\frac{1}{4},-\frac{1}{2}, 1, \ldots$
is -128 ?
questions.solution:
Since that given series are in G.P
Where first term $=\frac{1}{4}$, common ratio $=-2$
Let -128 is $n$th term
$\begin{array}{rlrl} 
& \therefore & -128 & =\frac{1}{4} \cdot(-2)^{n-1} \\
& & -128 \times 4 & =(-2)^{n-1} \\
\Rightarrow & & (-2)^9 & =(-2)^{n-1} \\
\Rightarrow & n & =9+1=10^{\text {th }}
\end{array}$

questions.solution:
$\sqrt{3}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}+\frac{1}{3 \sqrt{3}}+\ldots$
The given series is in G.P. an infinite series
Here, first term $=\sqrt{3}$
And common ratio $=\frac{1}{3}\therefore$ Required sum $=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{1-\frac{1}{3}}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{\frac{2}{3}}=\frac{3 \sqrt{3}}{2}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If an angle $\alpha$ is divided into two parts $A$ and $B$ such that $A-B=x$ and $\tan A: \tan B=2: 1$, then what is $\sinx$ equal to?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \text { Given that } \frac{\tan A}{\tan B}=\frac{2}{1} \\ & \begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \quad \frac{\sin A \cdot \cos B}{\cos A \cdot \sin B}=\frac{2}{1} \\ & \Rightarrow \quad \sin A \cdot \cos B-\cos A \cdot \sin B=\cos A \cdot \sin B\end{aligned} \\ & \begin{aligned} \sin (\mathrm{A}-\mathrm{B}) & =\frac{1}{2} \times 2 \cos A \cdot \sin B \\ & =\frac{1}{2}\{\sin (A+B)-\sin (A-B)\}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \quad \sin (\mathrm{A}-\mathrm{B})=\sin x=\frac{1}{2}(\sin \alpha-\sin x) \\ & \Rightarrow \quad 2 \sin x+\sin x=\sin \alpha \\ & \Rightarrow \quad \sin x=\frac{\sin \alpha}{3}\end{aligned}$
